name: Monte Sollube battlefield
story: Sollube (686 m) commands the coast road between Bermeo and Bilbao. In May 1937 it was attacked by the mixed Italian-Spanish Flechas Negras brigade under Sandro Piazzoni and the IV Navarrese Brigade, supported by the Condor Legion. Basque, Asturian and Cantabrian battalions defended it, including UGT, ANV and Kirikiño units. The mountain fell around 8 May, and fighting on its slopes continued for several days. Both sides suffered heavy casualties; published totals vary. Losing Sollube opened the coastal approach to Bilbao's Iron Belt and was seen at the time as the beginning of the end for the city's defence.
see: An open mountain with wide views to Bermeo and the Urdaibai estuary; any remains of positions are informal and unsigned.
plan: The BI-631 Bilbao–Bermeo road crosses the Sollube pass; short walks to the summit start from the pass.
